extracted.intended_audience: Executive branch agency officials, procurement and program managers, and legal/personnel staff responsible for make-or-buy decisions under OMB Circular A-76
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and standards for determining whether commercial or industrial-type work should be performed by contract (private sector) or in-house (Government) and for implementing inventory, review, cost-comparison, implementation, and appeals procedures across executive agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose: make-or-buy determination
rubrics_metrics.description: Sets the policies and procedures to determine whether needed commercial or industrial-type work should be done by contract (private sources) or in-house using Government facilities and personnel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to executive departments and agencies; replaces prior Circular A-76 and amendments; intended to implement consistent agency decisions about contracting vs. in-house performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Core policy precepts
rubrics_metrics.description: Three equally valid policy precepts: (1) rely on the private sector where available; (2) retain certain governmental functions in-house; (3) aim for economy via rigorous comparative cost analysis when private performance is feasible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These precepts guide all decisions under the Circular: reliance on private enterprise is default, but functions inherently governmental must be performed by Federal employees, and cost comparisons decide other cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Government commercial or industrial activity
rubrics_metrics.description: An activity operated and managed by a Federal executive agency that provides a product or service that could be obtained from a private source; must be separable from other functions and a regularly needed operational activity (not a one-time short-duration project).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes facility/equipment ownership aspects of GOCO facilities; a representative (not exhaustive) listing of such activities is provided in Attachment A.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Expansion (of activity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Modernization, replacement, upgrade, or expansion involving additional capital investment of $100,000 or more, or increasing annual operating costs by $200,000 or more, provided the increase exceeds 20% of total investment or operating cost.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consolidation of activities is not an 'expansion' unless thresholds are exceeded by the consolidated activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Conversion
rubrics_metrics.description: Transfer of work from a Government commercial or industrial activity to performance by a private commercial source under contract.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conversion decisions are governed by cost-comparison rules and other Circular provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: New start
rubrics_metrics.description: A newly-established Government commercial or industrial activity, including a transfer of work from contract to in-house performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New starts have special approval and savings thresholds (see New starts approval/savings criteria).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Private commercial source (geographic scope)
rubrics_metrics.description: A private business or other non-Federal activity located in the United States, its territories and possessions, the District of Columbia, or the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico which provides the commercial or industrial product or service required by Government agencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commercial cost figures must be based on bids/proposals from such private sources when used in comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Governmental function (must be in-house)
rubrics_metrics.description: Functions that must be performed in-house due to a special relationship in executing governmental responsibilities, including (1) discretionary application of Government authorities and value-judgment program management/selection, (2) monetary transactions and entitlements, and (3) minimum in-house/core R&D/testing capabilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Governmental functions are excluded from inventory and review requirements; ancillary or support activities beyond minimum core are not governmental functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope: overall applicability and exclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: No executive agency will engage in or contract for commercial or industrial activities except under this Circular or as otherwise provided by law; the Circular does not apply to governmental functions or to certain other categories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to GOCO facilities; does not authorize contracts where contracting authority otherwise does not exist; does not apply to establishing employer-employee relationships; additional limits described in paragraphs (d)(1)-(6).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope exclusion: employer-employee relationship prohibition
rubrics_metrics.description: Circular will not be used to enter into contracts which establish an employer-employee relationship between the Government and individual contract personnel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additional guidance found in Federal Personnel Manual (FPM) 300-8 and FPM 300-12.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope exclusion: not to avoid personnel ceilings or salary limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Circular will not be used to justify conversion to contract solely to meet personnel ceilings or to avoid salary limitations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When in-house performance is justified but would impact personnel ceilings, an appeal may be made to OMB for ceiling adjustment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope relationship to A-109 and consulting services
rubrics_metrics.description: Circular's relationship to OMB Circular A-109 (Major System Acquisitions) is clarified; Circular does not apply to consulting services that are purely advisory regarding governmental functions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should follow A-109 for major system acquisitions and executive-branch guidance on consulting services for purely advisory management assistance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of products/services from other Federal agencies (excess capacity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Excess property or services from other Federal agencies should be used in preference to new procurements; performing agency must justify operation of the activity and should not expand capacity without total workload review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When decision is based on comparative cost analysis, the using agency should solicit bids to establish commercial price and the performing agency should prepare the Government cost estimate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions authorizing Government operation: no satisfactory commercial source
rubrics_metrics.description: Government operation may be authorized when no satisfactory commercial source is available, subject to documentation and required notice/solicitation steps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency must place at least three notices over a 90-day period in the Commerce Business Daily (30 days with two notices in urgent cases); supplement outreach with GSA, SBA, and DOC assistance; urgency alone is not adequate; must document that contract performance would disrupt program if claimed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions authorizing Government operation: national defense/military necessity
rubrics_metrics.description: Government operation may be justified for combat support, retraining of military personnel, or mobilization readiness; Department of Defense will develop detailed criteria to be incorporated in implementing instructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Justifications must show why commercial performance would not meet the military need and require OMB approval for DoD-developed criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions authorizing Government operation: relative cost
rubrics_metrics.description: Government commercial or industrial activity may be authorized if a comparative cost analysis prepared in accordance with the Circular indicates the Government can provide the product or service at a cost lower than private commercial sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cost comparison principles and handbook guidance apply; see Cost Comparisons rubric.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost comparisons: common ground rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Comparative cost analyses must use the same scope of work and level of performance for both Government and commercial options, employ standard cost factors from the Cost Comparison Handbook, and consider all significant Government costs including overhead and indirect costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work statements must be sufficiently precise with performance standards; agencies must defend variations in costing; aim at full cost; use present value analysis when appropriate (OMB Circular A-94 discount rates).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost comparisons: base period and buy-in avoidance
rubrics_metrics.description: The base period for cost analysis should be keyed to the expected span of performance (usually the proposed contract period) to guard against 'buy-in' pricing; use of prepriced options and recompetition is recommended to avoid contract buy-in.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Base period corresponds to proposed contract unless circumstances dictate otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost comparisons: threshold for conducting studies
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies ordinarily should not conduct cost comparison studies to justify Government commercial or industrial activities for products or services estimated to cost the Government less than $100,000 per year, except when inadequate competition or unreasonable prices are suspected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reasonable efforts should first be made to obtain satisfactory prices from commercial sources and to develop competitive sources before conducting a study.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calculating contractor (commercial) costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Commercial cost figures must be based on a firm bid or proposal solicited in accordance with procurement regulations; bidders must be told an in-house cost estimate is being developed and that a contract may or may not result.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use solicitation to establish commercial price for comparison.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calculating Government operation costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must ensure Government operations are organized and staffed for the most efficient performance and include all significant costs; specified standard cost factors apply for retirement and insurance benefits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Government retirement cost factor (dynamic normal cost basis) = 20.4%; Government employee insurance (life and health) benefits cost factor = 4%; agencies may schedule internal reorganizations to achieve efficiency prior to cost comparison.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conversion and new-start savings thresholds
rubrics_metrics.description: Existing in-house activity will be converted to contract performance on the basis of economy only if it results in savings of at least 10% of estimated Government personnel costs. A 'new start' will not be approved on economy grounds unless savings are at least 10% of Government personnel costs plus 25% of equipment and facility costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These numeric thresholds must be applied in cost-comparison decisions; independent review of comparisons required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independent review of cost comparisons
rubrics_metrics.description: All cost comparisons must be reviewed by an activity independent of the cost analysis preparation to ensure conformance with instructions in the Cost Comparison Handbook.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Independent review ensures accuracy and consistency across agency decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implementation: agency responsibilities and organization
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency must designate an official at the assistant secretary level (or equivalent) to have overall responsibility for implementation, establish central contact offices with access to decision documents and data, and issue implementing regulations within 60 days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Copies of implementing regulations and subsequent changes must be forwarded to OMB's Office of Federal Procurement Policy for review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implementation: inventories, schedules, and notices
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must maintain inventories and an advance schedule for review of commercial and industrial activities and covered contracts; affected parties must be given at least 60 days' notice for major actions such as expansions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the number of activities/covered contracts is so great that reviews cannot be completed in prescribed periods, agencies may request OFPP/OMB approval to schedule reviews over a longer period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contract clauses and retention of decision records
rubrics_metrics.description: Contracts awarded as a result of Circular reviews must contain applicable clauses on equal employment opportunity, veterans' preference, minimum wages and fringe benefits; contractors must notify agencies of project changes, and actions/justifications are retained in agency inventory and made available upon request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These provisions protect rights of Federal employees, contractors, and other stakeholders.

rubrics_metrics.name: New starts: approval and budget timing
rubrics_metrics.description: New starts should not be initiated until justification has been reviewed and approved by a senior official; new starts involving capital investment or annual costs of $500,000 or more must be approved by the agency head or assistant secretary (or equivalent). Actions under this Circular should be completed before agency budget requests to OMB.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When government ownership of facilities is necessary, the possibility of contract operation must be considered before approving a new start; comparative cost decisions may be delayed to accommodate facility lead time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals: informal administrative review procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency must establish an informal administrative appeals procedure that provides, upon written request from a directly affected party, an independent objective review of determinations; expedited determinations must be made within 30 days by an official at the same or higher level than the approving official.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appeals procedures are meant to assure decisions are fair and in accordance with policy; they do not authorize appeals outside the agency or judicial review; procedures protect rights of Federal employees, representatives, contractors, and potential contractors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation and justification requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific explanations and documentation must accompany authorizations for government operation of commercial/industrial activities, especially if the function was previously performed by contract; differences in circumstances must be demonstrated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Justifications must spell out disruption claims in terms of cost, time, and performance measures and show disruptions are lasting/unacceptable; classified program, mission nature, or strike possibility alone are inadequate justifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Commerce Business Daily notices for market search
rubrics_metrics.description: Before concluding there is no satisfactory commercial source, agencies must place at least three notices over a 90-day period in the Commerce Business Daily (or two notices over 30 days for urgent requirements).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency efforts should especially solicit small and minority-owned businesses and use assistance from GSA, SBA, and DOC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attachment A: representative listing of commercial and industrial activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Attachment A provides a non-comprehensive list of activities considered commercial/industrial (e.g., audiovisual services, ADP, maintenance and repair, manufacturing, real property, transportation, printing, R&D, office services, security, food services, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The list is illustrative to help identify separable activities suitable for make-or-buy review; not exhaustive and not determinative of legal status in all cases.
